Metternich (Schemer) of Austria

  - Armistice (cease hostilities temporarily) — France and Austria

Assessment: GENEROUS

War Summary
The War for Bohemia: France holds Bohemia and Tyrol of Austria's; Britain holds Leon of ours.
War score: 52 ^ (Territory +10, Battle +15, Decisive Battle +10, Campaign +6, Blood +15, Ticking -4)
Settlement (this pair): Dictated Terms
Objective: Defense - the homeland — 28 of 28 provinces held (inactive)
Ticking: +0
Duration: 6 turns   Battles: 8W / 3L
Casualties: ours 29789 / theirs 78587
We hold: Bohemia, Tyrol

Armistice Terms
  A 5-turn ceasefire: fighting stops. The ledger stands: the war score reads +52 for France (11 battles, 1 decisive kept); the war is 6 turns old and stays so; exhaustion holds. No territory or gold changes hands until it ends.
  When it expires: a dictated peace on the held line if the loser reads -50 or worse with no hope left; otherwise peace if relations have healed to -60 or better; otherwise the war resumes at its age.
  At expiry: the war resumes where it stood — relations stand at -80 and will thaw to -65, short of -60; the ledger and the war's age come back with it.
  Austria's hope lives: Britain, Russia fight on, unspent.
  The cure is in reach: 1 turn of Improve Relations (+8 a turn, 1 DP) would carry this truce into peace.

  - Bavaria stays at war with Austria under this truce — an ally, not a client: her war runs on, and 3 French corps stand on Bavarian soil under the truce.
  - Our clients follow us out of the truce: Kingdom of Italy.
  - Austria sits outside your bloc. Peace normalizes relations with a nation resisting your European influence.

Metternich, with perfect politeness: "Vienna observes, with some weariness, that the fighting no longer serves even its winners. Grant the armistice. We will not pretend Marshal Ney's laurels at Bohemia count for nothing in this."

An interesting proposal. I shall study the terms closely.

This offer will lapse at end of turn.
